messages.content:
## Responses as Code

Each turn, you take your turn by calling the `submit_program` tool. Its `program`
string is run as one C# program: pass one whole, legal
C# program — bare code, with no code fences around it and no
prose inside it — and it is processed exactly as written. All calls are
synchronous.

`submit_program` is the only tool in this session, and every reply must call it.
Each call is acknowledged with a tool result reading `ok`; what the program
produced arrives as separate messages after it. Text you write alongside the
call is recorded, but nothing reads code out of it: only the `program` string
runs. If one reply makes several `submit_program` calls, the programs run
sequentially, in order, every one of them.

Your program is compiled by `csc` before it runs. A program it refuses
is not executed: you get its diagnostics and submit another program.

## Views

Views are the only way to read data out of your code and are provided on the
turn after they're opened. Print statements are not shown.

Reading images is not supported.

## Language Rules

Your program is compiled verbatim, as a whole compilation unit: the `using`
lines you need, then top-level statements.

## Ending your session

Turns continue until you end your session.

A program that fails does not end your session: the ending it called is revoked.
Fix the fault and end your session in a program that runs to completion.

Call `Gg.Session.Finish` with a short summary of what you did once the work is
complete.

## Your modules

Your program is given these modules:

- `Gg.Files`: Read, write, edit, list and walk the files of the workspace. — brought into scope with `using Gg;`
- `Gg.Shell`: Run shell commands in the workspace. — brought into scope with `using Gg;`
- `Gg.Docs`: Search this surface's own documentation, and take a documentation view back out. — brought into scope with `using Gg;`
- `Gg.Views`: Put a file, a computed value or an entry's documentation into the context window. — brought into scope with `using Gg;`
- `Gg.Session`: End the session, with a summary or with a reviewer's verdict. — brought into scope with `using Gg;`

Search the documentation to find a function, by keyword or by naming modules
above. Open a documentation view of each function you intend to call, and write
the call on a later turn.

The SDK declares every function, whatever this run enabled, so a call to one this
run withheld compiles and then fails when it runs, naming the call. What you can
find in the documentation is what you can call.

## Messages you receive

Every message you receive is headed by one of the following labels, on its own
line — a view's label is followed by `: ` and the name it was opened under; a
file view's by `: `, its path, `:`, the 1-based inclusive line range shown and
the file's total line count — followed by a `----` rule and then the content:

- `Task` — the task you are working on, or a message from a parent agent
- `Compiler error` — your last program did not compile, so none of it ran; the message is the compiler's error and nothing else. Fix it and resend the whole program
- `Runtime error` — your last program compiled and then threw, or was stopped by a sandbox limit; the message is the error and nothing else. Whatever the program did before it threw stands, so do not repeat that work
- `Notice` — a process notice from the harness (a mode change, or guidance)
- `Summary` — a summary standing in for older turns the harness compacted out of the window
- `Documentation` — documentation or a skill you asked to read, delivered on the following turn
- `File` — a file, or a window of one, shown in your context — seeded by the run or opened by your own file-view call — headed by its path, the 1-based line range shown and the file's total line count, as `File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines` (a whole file's range runs `1-N`)
- `View` — a value your program put into your window; the view's label follows the heading, as `View: changed-files`

For example, lines 100 to 250 of a 400-line file you opened a view of arrive
as:

```
File: src/main.ts:100-250 of 400 lines
----
...those lines of the file...
```

A program that ran is not announced: the views it opened are the result.

Task
----
Create the file `notes/plan.md` in the workspace. Its required content is specified in `specs/plan-brief.md`, which is already open in your context. Write the file exactly as the brief specifies.

Documentation: Gg.Docs.Search
----
Search(string? query = null, string[]? modules = null, string? type = null, Docs.DocKind? kind = null, uint? offset = null, uint? limit = null) -> Docs.DocPage
  query?: string? = null (passed by name) — The words to look for. Left out, the filters beside it are the whole of the search.
  modules?: string[]? = null (passed by name) — The modules to look in, each by gg's own id (`"views"`) or by the path this arm writes it as (`"Gg.Views"`). Several are a union: an entry in any one of them is a hit. Exact and case-insensitive; a name no module has matches nothing rather than failing. Left out, or empty, no module filter at all.
  type?: string? = null (passed by name) — One type's name, which narrows to that type and to the functions taking or returning it.
  kind?: Docs.DocKind? = null (passed by name) — Narrow to modules, to functions or to types. Left out, all three are searched.
  offset?: uint? = null (passed by name) — How many hits to skip. Left out, the page starts at the first.
  limit?: uint? = null (passed by name) — How many hits to return: 20 where it is left out, 100 at most, and zero refused.

Defined in `Gg.Docs`, brought into scope with `using Gg;`.

Find the calls this run offers, by keyword or by module, and read the briefs.

Matching is case-insensitive substring over names, signatures, briefs and detailed descriptions, so `"foobar"` finds `GetFoobar`. Hits are ranked by what matched: an entry whose own name carries the word comes before one that merely mentions it.

The filters compose with the query and with each other, and `modules` is a lookup rather than a search. A call with no query and no filter at all is refused. The page is returned as a value and is also opened as a view, and the next search replaces that view.

Returns: one page of matches, best first, and the total behind it.

Throws `ApiException`: `ApiErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for a call with no query and no filter beside it, and for a `limit` of zero.

Documentation: Gg.Views.OpenFile
----
OpenFile(string path, uint? offset = null, uint? limit = null, uint? maxLineChars = null) -> Files.FileRead
  path: string — The file to read and show, relative to the workspace or absolute.
  offset?: uint? = null (passed by name) — The 1-based first line. Left out, the whole file is shown.
  limit?: uint? = null (passed by name) — How many lines. Left out, the view runs to the end.
  maxLineChars?: uint? = null (passed by name) — The width, in characters, past which each line of the view is cut, from 1 to 65,536. Left out, lines arrive whole.

Defined in `Gg.Views`, brought into scope with `using Gg;`.

Read a file and show it in the context window.

The read's result is returned as well as shown. A view is keyed by the path and the region together, so two pages of one file are two views; opening the same page again replaces it.

A text view is capped at 65,536 bytes, and a file over the cap is refused rather than cut; the refusal names the size. Each line of the view longer than `maxLineChars` characters is cut there and annotated in place as `foo (123 more chars...)`, and the cap is measured after the cut. Only the view is cut: the returned value and the file itself are untouched. A picture is not subject to the cap.

Returns: the file's text window, or the picture's description.

Throws `ApiException`: `ApiErrorCode.NotFound` for a missing path, `ApiErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an offset past the end of the file or a width outside 1 to 65,536, and `ApiErrorCode.LimitExceeded`, naming the size, for a text view over 65,536 bytes. Nothing is opened when the read fails.
